title: Fill in the blank: branching
prompt: Fill in the instruction or condition each line needs: `csel`, `cset` and `cinc` pick a value with no branch, `cbz` guards a division, and an unsigned test skips the body of an if.

blanks.prompt: After cmp a_r, b_r, put the smaller of the two signed values in min_r with one instruction and no branch.
blanks.explanation: csel (conditional select) copies its first source when the condition holds and its second when it does not. lt holds when a_r < b_r, so min_r gets a_r then and b_r otherwise. When the two are equal either one is the smaller, so le would work as well.

blanks.prompt: After cmp w0, 0, write 1 to neg_r when w0 is negative and 0 when it is not.
blanks.explanation: cset (conditional set) turns a condition into a number: 1 when it holds and 0 when it does not. After cmp w0, 0, lt holds exactly when w0 is below 0.

blanks.prompt: Add 1 to hits_r only when the last cmp found its two values equal, and leave hits_r as it is otherwise.
blanks.explanation: cinc (conditional increment) writes its source plus 1 when the condition holds and the source unchanged when it does not. With eq it counts matches without a branch around an add.

blanks.prompt: Skip the division when the divisor in w20 is 0 by jumping to no_div, with no cmp in front.
blanks.explanation: cbz jumps when the register it names holds 0, and it needs no cmp. The guard matters because sdiv and udiv do not stop the program on a zero divisor: they quietly write 0 as the quotient.

blanks.prompt: idx_r and len_r hold unsigned values, and the C reads if (idx < len) { body }. After cmp idx_r, len_r, complete the branch that jumps past the body when the test is false.
blanks.explanation: To skip the body, branch on the complement of idx < len, which is idx >= len. For unsigned values that is hs (higher or same). cs (carry set) is another name for the same condition, and the assembler takes either spelling.
